```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

`dave_shiny()` explores OzFlux site outputs from DAVE in a Shiny app. You can
select repositories, sites, and outputs, then adjust the plot controls without
writing R code. For the same controls in R, see the [plotting
guide](plotting_dave.html). The examples below need your own DAVE repository
paths.

## Launch the explorer

Install the optional app dependencies and launch the explorer:

```{r launch-app}
install.packages(c("shiny", "plotly"))  # plotly >= 4.12.0
library(lpjguessOutput)
dave_shiny()
```

You can also pass repository paths at startup. All supplied repositories are
selected initially; names provide labels for the source dropdown:

```{r initial-sources}
dave_shiny(c(Baseline = "/path/to/dave", Experiment = "/path/to/dave2"))
```

The function returns a Shiny application object. In interactive sessions,
including RStudio, printing it opens the app in your default web browser. To
open the URL yourself, use:

```{r manual-browser}
dave_shiny(launch.browser = FALSE)
```

Automatic browser opening is disabled in non-interactive sessions. You can
also pass the application object to `shiny::runApp()`.

## Choose sources, sites, and outputs

Add repository directories (one path per line), select one or more sources,
then choose sites and outputs. These directories should be LPJ-GUESS DAVE
repositories, each containing paths such as:
`benchmarks/ozflux/<site>/out/<output>.out`.

Only sites present in every selected repository, and outputs present in every
selected repository/site pair are shown. Custom outputs without registered
metadata remain available under their filenames, but generated plots will not
have useful metadata such as units.

## Refresh output files

Fresh outputs are those modified within 10 seconds of the newest `.out` file in
each site's output directory by default. This timestamp heuristic excludes
leftover outputs from old runs. Empty and unreadable files are also excluded.
The **Files** tab shows each file's status.

Files are checked every five seconds and when **Refresh files** is clicked;
unchanged snapshots do not reload the data. Use `stale_threshold_secs` to change
the freshness window and `refresh_interval = 0` to disable periodic checks:

```{r refresh-settings}
dave_shiny("/path/to/dave", stale_threshold_secs = 30, refresh_interval = 0)
```

## Choose plot controls

The [output dimensions guide](output_dimensions.html) explains how model
identifiers and measured columns become facets, colours, and separate lines.

Choose data columns, one or more facets, a colour dimension, and shared or
independent y-axis scales. **Source** distinguishes repositories, while patch,
stand, PFT, individual, and soil layer dimensions are offered when present.
Initially, columns common to every selected file are selected; when outputs
have disjoint columns, all columns are selected explicitly. Metadata labels,
units, and soil depth labels use the same plotting code as `plot_dave()`.

## Inspect and export results

Preview the plotted data in **Data preview**, inspect output file statuses in
**Files**, or copy the equivalent `plot_dave()` call from **R code**. Download
the plotted data as CSV or save the plot as PNG or PDF.
